why: Count the ways: the last piece of a decoding is one digit or two digits, so ways[i] = ways[i-1] (if digit i-1 is 1..9) + ways[i-2] (if digits i-2..i-1 form 10..26). It is climbing stairs where some steps are forbidden.
hints: Look at the end of the string. The last letter came from either the last digit or the last two digits. When is each allowed?
ways[0] = 1 (empty prefix). ways[i] += ways[i-1] if s[i-1] != '0'; ways[i] += ways[i-2] if 10 <= int(s[i-2:i]) <= 26.
Keep only the last two values. O(n) time. A string that starts with 0 or contains '00' or '30' has 0 ways.
pitfalls: '0' alone is not a letter; '06' is not a valid two-digit code.
ways of the empty prefix is 1, not 0.
